newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank drains SKK400mln in tender, rate off.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank drains SKK400mln in tender, rate off.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Monday it had drained funds totalling 400 million crowns through a three-day securities reverse repurchase tender.
Peter Andresic, head of the NBS's Open Market Operation Department, told Reuters the only rate was 16.8 percent, after 17.3 percent for the previous reverse repo tender with a three-day maturity.
"It was the identical bid rate by commercial banks, perhaps signalling they are willing to lower interest rates. I have nothing to add to it on the NBS's behalf," he said.
He added the NBS tender was fully subscribed, with all 400 million crowns worth of bids being accepted.

Interbank money market dealers had said they were eyeing the NBS for a possible repo rate cut or some other measures affecting rates after Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said this week that steps were being taken to lower rates.
The government also appointed former deputy finance minister Jozef Magula this week to the bank board, which had made analysts wary of possible policy changes at the meeting.
Andresic said he was not aware of any imminent policy changes at the central bank.
